facts.fact_text: The present case concerns the first applicant's static demonstration in November 2009.

The first applicant submitted a notice to the Gelendzhik municipality notifying them of his intention to hold a static demonstration on 26 November 2009 near the town office of the Federal Security Service (FSB).
On 26 November 2009 the first applicant held the demonstration as planned.
By a judgment of 15 December 2009, a justice of the peace convicted the first applicant under Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The justice of the peace sentenced the first applicant to a fine of 2,000 Russian roubles (approximately 45 euros at the time).

The justice of the peace held that the first applicant had committed a breach of public order on account of his failure to abstain from holding the demonstration despite the lawful warning document issued by the Gelendzhik municipality.
The justice of the peace stated that the first applicant's actions amounted to 'putting pressure on justice in relation to a specific criminal case'.

The Gelendzhik Town Court of the Krasnodar Region stated that the goal of the first applicant's demonstration amounted to indirect interference with the administration of justice in the criminal case against Mr Ivanov.

On 23 November 2009, referring to section 12 § 2 of the Public Events Act (Federal Law no. 54-FZ of 19 June 2004) and Article 294 of the Criminal Code, the Gelendzhik municipality issued a warning document to the first applicant.

Pursuant to Federal Law no. 54-FZ of 19 June 2004 (the Public Events Act), a public event may be held in any convenient location, provided that it does not create a risk of building collapse or any other risks to the safety of the participants (section 8 § 1).

Under section 12 § 2 of Federal Law no. 54-FZ of 19 June 2004 (the Public Events Act), if the information contained in the notification or other factors give reason to believe that the aims of the public event or the manner of its conduct are contrary to the Constitution, the Criminal Code or the Code of Administrative Offences, the competent regional or municipal authority must warn the organisers in writing that they may be held liable for any unlawful actions, in accordance with the procedure prescribed by law.

By two decisions of 3 October 2011, an unspecified judge of Oktyabrskiy District Court of Novorossiysk authorised the tapping of the applicants' conversations on three mobile telephone numbers.
The authorisation for tapping the applicants' conversations on three mobile telephone numbers was granted from 3 October 2011 for 180 days.

The decision of 3 October 2011 in respect of the second applicant mentioned that, according to information held by the FSB office of the Krasnodar Region, the second applicant was the subject of investigative file no. 543 (дело оперативного учета).

The decision of 3 October 2011 in respect of the second applicant mentioned that data obtained in respect of him indicated that he had been involved in the organisation of an extremist community, which is an offence under Article 282.1 of the Criminal Code.
By a judgment of 30 April 2013, the Town Court convicted the applicants as charged.
In its judgment of 30 April 2013, the Town Court held that the interception of the applicants' communications had been lawful and thus the records could be relied on as evidence.
In its judgment of 30 April 2013, the Town Court held that no circumstance was identified for rejecting the records of intercepted communications as inadmissible evidence.

In its judgment of 30 April 2013, the Town Court rejected the defendants' argument that the records of the intercepted telephone communications should not be used in evidence because during the preliminary investigation the investigator did not receive court decisions authorising the interception.

In its judgment of 30 April 2013, the Town Court rejected the defendants' argument that the records of the intercepted telephone communications should not be used in evidence because the court decisions did not bear the seal of the authorising court.

The Town Court noted in its judgment of 30 April 2013 that under section 13 of the Instruction of 17 April 2007, operational-search activities results arising from the interception of telephone communications should be accompanied by a copy of the related court decisions authorising the operational-search activities.
The Town Court noted in its judgment of 30 April 2013 that an authorised official certified the copies of court decisions nos. 706 and 707 and apposed an appropriate seal.

The Town Court held in its judgment of 30 April 2013 that the court decisions were requested and admitted to the file in compliance with Articles 271 and 286 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, section 11 of the Operational-Search Activities Act and paragraphs 11 and 21 of the Instruction of 17 April 2007.

The Town Court held in its judgment of 30 April 2013 that the fact that court decisions nos. 706 and 707 were not handed over to the investigator during the investigation does not tarnish the operational-search activities results.

The first applicant submitted a notice to the Gelendzhik municipality notifying them of his intention to hold a static demonstration on 26 November 2009 near the town office of the Federal Security Service (FSB).

On 23 November 2009, referring to section 12 § 2 of the Public Events Act (Federal Law no. 54-FZ of 19 June 2004) and Article 294 of the Criminal Code, the Gelendzhik municipality issued a warning document to the first applicant.
The warning document issued by the Gelendzhik municipality on 23 November 2009 invited the first applicant to abstain from holding the planned demonstration.
The warning document issued by the Gelendzhik municipality on 23 November 2009 indicated that if the demonstration were to be held, the first applicant and participants might be held liable.
On 26 November 2009 the first applicant held the demonstration as planned.
